items.headline: Parliament marks a year since Cyclone Ditwah
items.summary: Parliament observed a moment of silence for the victims on the cyclone's first anniversary. Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa called for a disaster system built on preparedness and asked whether relief from the Rs. 500 billion supplementary estimate had reached affected farmers, fishers and small traders.

items.headline: Rs. 10,000 extra for police; 65,000 seek e-bikes
items.summary: Public Security Minister Ananda Wijepala said police food and accommodation allowances will go up from Rs. 28,200 to Rs. 38,200 because a separate risk allowance could not fit in this year's budget. About 65,000 officers have applied for government-backed electric motorcycles, which will come with interest-free loans.

items.headline: Airbus probe investigator to testify in Namal case
items.summary: A French forensic accountant who helped uncover the Airbus bribery network is expected to testify, together with an Airbus vice-president, in the case against MP Namal Rajapaksa. Prosecutors allege a US$16 million kickback on a proposed US$2.3 billion SriLankan Airlines aircraft deal.

items.headline: Navy seizes drug boat south of Dondra
items.summary: The Navy detained a vessel with no flag and seven suspects in international waters. The boat is believed to have been carrying heroin and crystal meth, and the suspects are being brought ashore for the Police Narcotics Bureau.

items.headline: Heavy rain over 100 mm in five provinces
items.summary: Heavy falls above 100 mm are likely in parts of the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central, Southern and Uva provinces. People are asked to watch for lightning and sudden strong winds, and seas off several coasts may be rough.

items.headline: Herath and Jaishankar meet in Delhi
items.summary: Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath met India's S. Jaishankar ahead of the IORA Council of Ministers meeting. They discussed bilateral ties and the regional situation.

items.headline: Caucus weighs action on deported sex offenders
items.summary: The Women Parliamentarians' Caucus looked at ways to act against citizens deported after sexual abuse convictions abroad. Ideas included recognising foreign judgments, sharing conviction data internationally and requiring background checks for child-care staff.

items.headline: 27-acre arts and cultural village proposed
items.summary: A Cabinet paper seeks approval to acquire land near Colombo for a village housing film, arts, meditation and Buddhist studies institutions.

items.headline: Fewer public servants, bigger salary bill
items.summary: The public service shrank by about 23,300 staff to 893,797 in the year to June. Salary spending still rose 8.7% to Rs. 827 billion in the first eight months of 2026, largely because of the pay revision.

items.headline: Rupee slips again against the dollar
items.summary: Most banks raised their dollar rates by 20–25 cents. Selling rates are around Rs. 337–337.75.

items.headline: Sallay petition order put off to January 28
items.summary: The Court of Appeal postponed its decision on whether to hear former SIS chief Suresh Sallay's challenge to his PTA detention order linked to the Easter attacks probe.

items.headline: Senior DIG Pathinayake at Bribery Commission
items.summary: Senior DIG Lalith Pathinayake, who oversees the Central Province, went to the Bribery Commission to give a statement in an ongoing inquiry.

items.headline: Shark fins traded for kendu leaves off Chilaw
items.summary: The Coast Guard and Navy arrested four Sri Lankan and three Indian fishermen during an at-sea swap. They seized about 180 kg of shark fins and 1,890 kg of kendu leaves.

items.headline: Three killed on roads; arrest in bank fraud
items.summary: A toddler was among three people killed in separate crashes in Embilipitiya, Dambulla and Homagama. Separately, a 25-year-old data entry officer was arrested over a Rs. 1 million fake banking website scam.

items.headline: Double cricket success for Sri Lanka
items.summary: Sri Lanka A beat India A by eight wickets to reach the Asia Cup Rising Stars final in Doha. The women's side finished unbeaten to win the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy.

items.headline: Amnesty presses for accountability after UN report
items.summary: Amnesty International said a new UN rights office report on crimes during the war shows little progress on justice and that impunity persists. It urged continued international scrutiny.
